summary: This 4-page manuscript presents a machine-checked Lean 4.35.0 kernel (18 constructive theorems, zero external dependencies, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) and a zero-floating-point exact-rational certificate verifier (KOSZUL-WORDLE-CERT-1.0) auditing the finite homological, Euler-characteristic, counterexample, and zero-set evaluation-rank core of Smithline (2026, arXiv:2611.33113) on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. All algebraic identities, generating-function dimension counts, Koszul alternating sums, parity obstructions, and strictness-defect grid values reported in the PDF are mathematically sound and mutually consistent, and the authors honestly scope out the general mapping-cone induction (Theorem 5.1) and game-theoretic construction (Theorem 1.1). While modest in theoretical scope and missing printed Lean theorem type signatures in the PDF, the work is solid, rigorous, and free of material errors.
weaknesses: The Lean 4 formalization covers only grade-2 and grade-3 Koszul differential square-zero properties and conditional Euler-characteristic telescoping rather than arbitrary-grade Koszul complexes or concrete instance exactness inside Lean (exactness of concrete complexes is verified only by the Python auditor).

Because the 4-page PDF reports only theorem identifiers and axiom footprints (Table 1) without printing the formal Lean 4 type signatures or quantifiers, an external reader of the PDF alone cannot inspect the exact formal definitions underlying identifiers such as `koszul_exactness_euler_char_list` or `feasible_history_dim_bound`.
Empirical evaluation in Mode 4 is restricted to s_k in {1,2} (to keep V(J_n) rational) and small problem sizes (up to |V|=48, 48x64 matrices).
